title: Book record
description: PROPOSED, pending Samuel's review. What a textbook prints for one lesson, one record per printed thing. The same format for ground truth (records a person has confirmed) and for ingestion (records an extractor produced), so the two can be compared record by record. Only what the book prints belongs here; generated or expert content (worked-out answers, wrong answers, misconceptions, prerequisites, answer-checker settings) belongs to a separate teaching layer that references these ids. Rules this schema cannot express (id scheme, counting, references that must resolve) are in README.md and checked by validate.py.

_about.description: Free-text note, used by example files only.

role.description: ground_truth: built and checked by people against the book; every item must carry a quote. extraction: produced by an extractor; an anchor may stand in for the quote.

open_questions.description: Questions about the book that a person must settle.

history.description: Log of changes to the file, one line each.

text.description: Markdown with maths as $...$, in the book's printed form (a printed decimal comma stays a comma; a misprint stays as printed and is recorded in misprints).

record_id.description: <lesson slug>:<local id>. Local ids follow README 'Ids': the printed label and number (example-2, drill-3), or the type and a lesson-wide count (rule-4). Frozen once the record is reviewed.

page.description: Printed page number (PDF page = printed page + source_document.page_offset).

provenance.description: Who or what produced the record.

by.description: Extractor and version (e.g. 'extraction line v2, b8-1') or the person who drafted it, and date.

review.description: A person's review of one record. Absent = not reviewed.

reason.description: Required when flagged: what needs someone else's decision.

fields.description: Fields changed, or e.g. 'type: rule → learning_objective', 'added'.

file_path.description: Repo-relative path of the PDF (docs/Source/...); the PDFs themselves are not in git.

text_layer.description: Whether the PDF has usable text, e.g. 'usable', 'partial', 'empty, drawn as images'.

module.description: The unit or chapter, as printed.

notation.description: Where a printed form needs reading: the form as printed and what it means. Not for misprints.

misprint.description: A mistake the book prints, confirmed by a person. The record keeps the printed form; the scorer accepts either reading at this spot; the teaching layer uses the intended one. Spelling slips in prose that change no meaning are transcribed as printed and need no entry.

field.description: Where in this record the misprint sits, e.g. 'quote', 'stem', 'solution[1]', 'caption', 'rows[2][1]'.

notes.description: How we know, e.g. 'the table beside it shows (3, a)'.

part.description: One printed part of an exercise, activity, prompt or worked example. Identified by <item id>:<label>. Parts are flat: a nested printed label is joined with a space as printed ('First A').

label.description: As printed (a, b, A, 1, ...); nested labels joined with a space ('First A').

answer.description: Only when the book prints it.

answer_figure.description: Figure or table record(s) holding a printed answer that is a drawing.

code.description: Publisher's practice code printed instead of an answer (Siyavula).

solution_provenance.description: book_printed: answer printed in the student book; book_worked: a worked example's printed solution; book_online: the publisher's answer behind a printed practice code.

item.description: One printed thing on the lesson's pages.

type.description: Statements (claim): definition, rule, caution, convention, method (a printed method box only). Prompts (text + parts): exercise, activity, open_prompt (a printed 'Why?'/'Think' with no printed answer). worked_example (stem + solution + answer). figure (caption), table (caption + rows), key_term (term), printed_objective (text). Structure (text): heading (a printed section heading), linking_text (prose that leads between items), prior_knowledge.

lo.description: The learning objective this item teaches.

belongs_to.description: The item this one is printed as part of: a figure or table inside an example, a labelled prompt inside an example's frame.

quote.description: A few exact printed words that locate the item, misprints included. The book's full text is not copied. Required in ground-truth files.

header.description: Table only: the printed column headings, left to right, including the corner cell.

rows.description: Table only: each printed row, left to right, row label first. Cells as printed.

examples.description: Examples the book lists with a statement.

answer_figure.description: Figure or table record(s) holding a printed answer that is a drawing.

learning_objective.description: A 'can do' objective the pages teach. Not printed as such (except printed_objective items), but kept here because extraction produces them and scoring needs them next to their evidence. Its pages are the pages of its evidence items; it has no page of its own.

label.description: Short name a student would recognise.

order_in_parent.description: Position in the book's teaching order.

evidence.description: Ids of the items that teach it; review asks for at least two of different types.
